case_name: Smt Kiran Bala vs Jugal Kumar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt Kiran Bala, complainant in Ct. Case No.511800/16

facts_of_case: Complainant seeks leave to appeal against judgment acquitting respondent of offence under section 494 IPC.

legal_principles.principle: Saptapadi is not an essential ingredient of a Hindu marriage.
legal_principles.held: Mr. Jain submits however, that saptapadi is not an essential ingredient of a Hindu marriage;

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to prove that saptapadi was part of customary rites and ceremonies or that without saptapadi, no marriage was contracted.
legal_principles.held: Counsel submits that in any case, it was a matter of defence for the respondent to prove that saptapadi was part of such customary rites and ceremonies or that without saptapadi, no marriage was contracted.

legal_principles.principle: The statement of the second wife's father, Kishan Swaroop, is admissible as evidence.
legal_principles.held: It is further pointed-out that, in fact the second wife's father Kishan Swaroop has admitted in his statement recorded as CW-2 on 06.12.2017 that...

outcome.final_order: Exemption granted, subject to just exceptions. Let requisite compliances be made within 01 week.

appealing an acquittal in a criminal case
seeking leave to appeal under Section 378(4) of Cr.P.C
